svg.title: The Lorentz factor gamma, explained
svg.desc: Beta is a bar's step as a fraction of the speed limit. Gamma = 1 / sqrt(1 - beta squared) stays near 1 for slow bars and shoots up near the limit. Marked: the values printed by the lorentz_basics example and the betas of the real timelike SPY bars.
svg.text: The Lorentz factor γ: how close a bar came to the limit

text.tspan: = step ÷ c, a speed from 0 to 1.

svg.text: Slow bars get γ ≈ 1. Near the limit γ shoots up, like a particle near light speed.
srfm --backtest sizes each position by γ, clamped to 1x to 3x
β (step as a fraction of the speed limit)
Teal ticks: β of the 295 timelike SPY daily bars (median β 0.72, γ 1.45).
